transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because things at home have gotten really hard since my in-laws moved in with us. I feel keyed up all the time and worn down, and it’s starting to affect how I act. I’ve been snapping at my wife, avoiding calls I’d normally take care of right away, and at work I almost let a musician’s contract fall apart because I just couldn’t think straight.
Have you been feeling anxious lately?

Yes. Since my in-laws moved into our house, I’ve been really keyed up and worn down. I’m snapping at my wife, avoiding calls I’d normally handle right away, and I almost let a musician’s contract fall apart because I just couldn’t think straight.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed lately?
I don’t know if I’d call it depressed. I’ve been more stressed and worn out than anything. Sad sometimes, I guess, but that hasn’t felt like the main thing.
Have you had any panic attacks recently?
I don’t think so. I’ve felt really anxious and tense, but I haven’t had anything I’d call a panic attack.
Are you avoiding any specific social situations or activities because of how you've been feeling?

Yeah, I’ve been avoiding calls I’d normally take care of right away. It’s not really social events so much as work stuff—I just feel so keyed up and worn down that I put things off, and it’s causing problems. I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart because I couldn’t think straight.
Have you been having any recurring thoughts or urges to repeat certain behaviors?
No, not really. I haven’t noticed any urges like that or needing to repeat things.
Have you been feeling like you need to do things in a specific way or order to feel okay?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed needing things done in a certain order or feeling like something bad will happen if I don’t do it that way.
Have you been having any intrusive thoughts that keep repeating in your mind?
I don’t think so. I mean, I have worries on my mind, but not intrusive thoughts that repeat over and over like that.
Do you feel compelled to perform specific rituals or behaviors to relieve your anxiety?
No, I don’t think so. I get anxious, but I’m not doing any specific rituals or routines to make it go away.
Do you feel like you're doing more checking or double-checking than you used to?
Not really. I might check something once in a while like anyone would, but I haven’t noticed myself double-checking things more than I used to.
Have you been having any thoughts that keep coming back into your mind even when you try to focus on something else?
No, not in that way. I mean, I have worries and stuff on my mind, but I don’t have thoughts that keep forcing their way back in when I’m trying to focus.
Do you feel an overwhelming need to control or regulate your environment in any way?
No, I don’t think so. I like things to be manageable, but I don’t feel an overwhelming need to control everything around me or keep my environment a certain way.
Do you feel like you're doing anything over and over to try to make your anxiety better?
No, I don’t think I’m doing anything repeatedly like that. I might try to calm myself down or step away from something stressful, but not in a ritual or repeated way to make the anxiety go away.
Have you been feeling like you need to repeat certain actions to reduce your anxiety?
No, I haven’t noticed anything like that. I don’t feel like I have to repeat certain actions to calm myself down.
Are you avoiding any places or situations because you fear something might happen to you or someone else?
No, I don’t think so. I’m not really avoiding places because I’m afraid something will happen to me or someone else.
Do you have any thoughts that you feel are unreasonable or disturbing, but that keep coming back into your mind?
Not really. I mean, I have worries that come back, but I wouldn’t say they feel disturbing or unreasonable in that way. It’s more just stress on my mind.
Do you have any recurring thoughts that you try to ignore or suppress?
I’m not sure I’d call them thoughts I’m trying to suppress. I do get things stuck in my head sometimes, but I don’t feel like I’m fighting off disturbing thoughts or anything like that.
Do you feel like you're doing anything to try to neutralize or undo your anxious thoughts?
No, I don’t think I’m doing anything like that. I might try to distract myself or stay busy when I’m anxious, but I’m not doing rituals or trying to “undo” thoughts, if that’s what you mean.
Is your anxiety primarily focused on your current situation with your in-laws, or do you find yourself worrying about a wide range of things in general?

It’s mostly about the situation at home with my in-laws. Since they moved in, I’ve just been really keyed up and worn down. I’m snapping at my wife, and it’s spilling into work too—I’ve been avoiding calls I’d normally handle right away, and I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart because I couldn’t think straight.
Has your anxiety started to improve at all since you've been dealing with the stress of your in-laws moving in?

Not really, no. I mean, the situation is still going on—they’re still living with us—so it doesn’t feel like there’s been much chance for things to settle down. The stress is still pretty active day to day.
